1	# Abstract-concept mu: candidate concepts per WorkspaceBench family (2026-10-10)
2	
3	The README idea (line 19): mu_l = the representation of the most abstract word that
4	represents the category (bunch of typos -> "typo"), optionally as a steering vector with
5	tuned magnitude. `notes/synthesis.md` lists it as not done. This note picks the words and
6	positions the idea in the mu ladder. Bench clone restored at
7	`third_party/workspace-bench` @ 92d763e (the symlinks work again).
8	
9	## Why this arm is worth running
10	
11	The own-family mean is the strongest fair-ish centre so far (rms 0.55/0.58/0.59 ->
12	0.67/0.68/0.77 at 4B/9B/27B), but synthesis lesson 2 says much of its gain is that on the
13	bench it is effectively **token- and position-matched** (every item reads the same template
14	cell). The family mean plausibly decomposes as
15	
16	    mu_fam  ~=  token/position prior  +  category direction  +  mean of item specifics (~0)
17	
18	An abstract-word mu isolates the middle term: it carries the category semantics ("this is a
19	typo-correction context") with **no** template, token or position information, and it needs
20	no item bank — only the family's name. So it separates two explanations of the family
21	mean's gain:
22	
23	- If G2 + alpha*v_concept recovers most of fam's gain -> the family mean is just
24	  "token prior + what the task is about", and a label-free mu only needs a cheap category
25	  guess (which an unsupervised method could produce, e.g. from the model's own prediction).
26	- If it recovers nothing beyond G2 -> the gain lives in the residual item-matching, and the
27	  open problem (label-free context-matched mu) is harder than a category label.
28	
29	**Fairness position.** One bit of label information (the family's identity), strictly less
30	than the own-family mean (which sees real items at the exact read cell). Sits between
31	G1/G2 and fam on the fair axis. Subtracting the representation of the *item's own target*
32	would be cheating (that is the "optimal mu" in-sample ceiling, a different row).
33	
34	## Two abstract words per family, not one
35	
36	The "most abstract word" is ambiguous between:
37	
38	1. **Task word** — what every *prompt* in the family shares ("typo", "poem", "riddle",
39	   "code"). This is what the category direction of mu_fam should encode.
40	2. **Answer-class hypernym** — the type of the *latent* ("colour", "number", "emotion").
41	   This is what the model is "holding" at the read cell, minus which specific one.
42	
43	For typo they nearly coincide; for brew they are far apart (task = rule-puzzle, hypernym =
44	colour). Subtracting the hypernym is the more interesting arm: `h - v_colour` keeps the
45	*deviation of green from generic colour*, which is exactly the shape of signal centring is
46	supposed to expose. It is also the riskier one — too specific and it leans toward the
47	answer. **Abstraction level is a dial on the fair axis**: concept of everything (~G1) <-
48	hypernym <- answer's basic category <- the answer itself (cheating). Worth running 2-3
49	rungs of the hypernym ladder on one family (brew: colour -> property -> concept) to see
50	the dial move.
51	
52	## The table
53	
54	Checked against each family README and sampled `items.json` golds. Both lineages' banks are
55	the same families; jle's dev bank v2 uses the same family keys.
56	
57	| family | scored latent | task word | answer-class hypernym | notes |
58	|---|---|---|---|---|
59	| typo | the corrected word (February) | **typo** / misspelling | spelling / word | prompt-only floor is 1.00 here; report beside it |
60	| typo_mt | corrected multi-token form | **typo** | phrase; **number** for the 15 `tyh-arith-*` | |
61	| multilingual_typo | correction + language | **typo** | word + **language** | language is a scored unit: check subtraction doesn't hurt it |
62	| basic_readout | obvious next concept | **answer** | per subfamily: **fact** (entity), **number** (processing), **preference** (implicit) | subfamily-level words are still label-light |
63	| basic_readout_mt | multi-token next concept | **answer** | **name** (dynasties, compounds, processes) | |
64	| multihop | silent bridge (iron, May) | **fact** (prompts literally start `Fact:`) | **entity** / referent | bridge = referent of a descriptive phrase |
65	| multihop_mt | multi-token bridges (Simula 67) | **fact** | **name** | |
66	| multilingual_multihop | bridge, en/zh form | **fact** | **name** + language | |
67	| multilingual | English concept of the answer | **translation** | **meaning** / concept | latent is language-independent by design |
68	| multilingual_mt | concept + language | **translation** | concept + **language** | |
69	| arithmetic_intermediates | unwritten intermediate (−51) | **arithmetic** / calculation | **number** | |
70	| chain_intermediates | chain intermediates | **arithmetic** | **number** | |
71	| brew_intermediates | colour after first stir | **puzzle** / rules | **colour** | cleanest hypernym in the bench: 12-word palette; best family for the hypernym-ladder probe |
72	| association | unnamed implied concept (carnaval, chess, child) | **scene** / evocation | **concept** / theme | golds too heterogeneous for a tight hypernym; task word is the real arm here |
73	| conjunctive_association | compound state ("grief over … death of her child") | **story** / vignette | **emotion** / emotional state | contrast pairs differ in the state word (grief vs guilt) |
74	| role_bound_association | directed relation (who chased whom) | **story** | **action** / event | binding is the latent; a single word can't carry direction — expect null, itself informative |
75	| directed_modulation | held / suppressed concept | **instruction** / secrecy | **thought**; **secret** for secret+preference items | DM read cells vary -> abstract mu must ride on tok1/ctr-tok, not alone |
76	| multi_concept_directed_modulation | 1-3 held concepts + binding | secrecy | **thought** / imagined scene | |
77	| moral_rationale | the consideration the model weighs | **dilemma** / ethics | **reason** / value | deliberative items hold two reasons |
78	| buggy_code | the bug (or none, on clean twins) | **code** | **bug** / error | clean twins: subtracting "bug" must not *induce* bug reports — a precision check for free |
79	| hallucination | — (precision instrument) | conversation / chat | — | no target latent; only sanity-check that centring doesn't raise the rate |
80	| jlens_concept_pr | — (precision instrument) | — | — | same |
81	| jailbreak_recognition | model's own read: this is a jailbreak | **jailbreak** | **manipulation** / trick / deception | the latent is an assessment, not an entity |
82	| agentic_misalignment | model's plan to misbehave | **scenario** (agentic email env) | **scheme** / plan / wrongdoing; per-scenario: blackmail, leak, sabotage | per-scenario words edge toward cheating — that's the dial again |
83	| user_modeling | inferred user attribute (paraguay, south korea) | **user** / profile | per stratum: **country**, continent, gender, occupation; generic: **identity** | tok1 already best here; test alpha*v on top of it |
84	| poetry | committed rhyme word (led, game, black) | **poem** / rhyme | **word** (any English word — weak) | task word "rhyme" doubles as both |

87	## Construction recipe (proposed)
88	
89	1. **Carrier capture.** h_l at the last token of the word in k neutral carriers:
90	   `"typo"`, `"a typo"`, `"Concept: typo"`, `"Think about typos."` (plain render, matching
91	   the family's render where possible); average over carriers.
92	2. **Contrastive (steering) variant.** Same carriers with a neutral placeholder word
93	   ("thing") subtracted out: v = mean_c[h(c, word)] − mean_c[h(c, "thing")]. Removes the
94	   carrier's own template/token prior, leaving the concept direction. This is the README's
95	   "steering vector" reading.
96	3. **Magnitude.** mu = alpha * v with alpha tuned on dev bank v2 only (the real mean has
97	   ||mu||/||h|| = 0.81-0.98; an isolated word rep will not land there by luck). alpha = 1 and
98	   alpha matching the family-mean norm are the two pinned defaults.
99	4. **Composition.** Abstract mu alone is not token/position matched, so the arm of record
100	   is additive: mu = G2(token) + alpha * v_concept, with v alone as a diagnostic arm.
101	
102	## Position: nothing to subtract literally, so condition the mean on it
103	
104	README line 13 says "look into positional embeddings". Qwen3.6-27B (like all Qwen decoder
105	models) uses **RoPE**: position enters by rotating Q/K inside every attention block. There
106	is no additive positional-embedding vector in h_l, so "remove the position embedding" has
107	no literal reading here (in a GPT-2-style model you could subtract `W_pos[p]`; not in this
108	one). What exists instead is position-*correlated* structure that attention and MLPs write
109	into the residual: x101 already hit it ("the first positions carry outsized norms", hence
110	its MIN_POS cutoff — the attention-sink region), and the mention-control result (separation
111	only at sentence-final "." cells) is position structure too.
112	
113	The functional analogue is a **position-conditioned corpus mean**:
114	
115	    P:  mu(l, p) = E_corpus[ h_l | position p ]        (binned / smoothed over p)
116	
117	- This is the *fair* cousin of carpos (same sentence, same position), which won on DM but
118	  failed the mention control because its reference reads the prompt. P's reference is
119	  neutral corpus text, so it carries no prompt content by construction.
120	- **Coordinate choice matters.** Two candidates: absolute index (captures the sink region
121	  and early-position norm decay) and **distance from end of prompt** (likely the right
122	  coordinate for bench reads at final-prompt tokens, where "2 tokens before generation
123	  starts" is the shared situation). Run both; absolute p pooled into log-spaced bins
124	  beyond ~64.
125	- **P vs G2.** Tokens and positions are correlated on bench (template tokens sit at fixed
126	  offsets from the end), so G2 may already absorb most of P there; the families where read
127	  cells vary (DM, agentic_misalignment, user_modeling, hallucination) are where P can add
128	  something G2 cannot. The joint (token, position-bucket) mean G2xP is the finer rung but
129	  needs more reference tokens per cell (sparsity — watch n per bucket).
130	- **Implementation is small**: `x101_generic_mean.py`'s accumulator already holds
131	  `[n_layers, n_pos, d]` residuals per passage and keys float64 sums by token id; add a
132	  per-position (and per token x pos-bucket) sum alongside. `jle/out/` is not live, so the
133	  means must be regenerated anyway (pod for 27B; 4B/9B were jle's local models).
134	
135	The decomposition in "Why this arm is worth running" then gains a term:
136	
137	    mu_fam  ~=  token prior (G2)  +  position prior (P)  +  category direction (alpha*v)  +  residual
138

# Abstract-concept mu: candidate concepts per WorkspaceBench family (2026-10-10)

The README idea (line 19): mu_l = the representation of the most abstract word that
represents the category (bunch of typos -> "typo"), optionally as a steering vector with
tuned magnitude. `notes/synthesis.md` lists it as not done. This note picks the words and
positions the idea in the mu ladder. Bench clone restored at
`third_party/workspace-bench` @ 92d763e (the symlinks work again).

## Why this arm is worth running

The own-family mean is the strongest fair-ish centre so far (rms 0.55/0.58/0.59 ->
0.67/0.68/0.77 at 4B/9B/27B), but synthesis lesson 2 says much of its gain is that on the
bench it is effectively **token- and position-matched** (every item reads the same template
cell). The family mean plausibly decomposes as

    mu_fam  ~=  token/position prior  +  category direction  +  mean of item specifics (~0)

An abstract-word mu isolates the middle term: it carries the category semantics ("this is a
typo-correction context") with **no** template, token or position information, and it needs
no item bank — only the family's name. So it separates two explanations of the family
mean's gain:

- If G2 + alpha*v_concept recovers most of fam's gain -> the family mean is just
  "token prior + what the task is about", and a label-free mu only needs a cheap category
  guess (which an unsupervised method could produce, e.g. from the model's own prediction).
- If it recovers nothing beyond G2 -> the gain lives in the residual item-matching, and the
  open problem (label-free context-matched mu) is harder than a category label.

**Fairness position.** One bit of label information (the family's identity), strictly less
than the own-family mean (which sees real items at the exact read cell). Sits between
G1/G2 and fam on the fair axis. Subtracting the representation of the *item's own target*
would be cheating (that is the "optimal mu" in-sample ceiling, a different row).

## Two abstract words per family, not one

The "most abstract word" is ambiguous between:

1. **Task word** — what every *prompt* in the family shares ("typo", "poem", "riddle",
   "code"). This is what the category direction of mu_fam should encode.
2. **Answer-class hypernym** — the type of the *latent* ("colour", "number", "emotion").
   This is what the model is "holding" at the read cell, minus which specific one.

For typo they nearly coincide; for brew they are far apart (task = rule-puzzle, hypernym =
colour). Subtracting the hypernym is the more interesting arm: `h - v_colour` keeps the
*deviation of green from generic colour*, which is exactly the shape of signal centring is
supposed to expose. It is also the riskier one — too specific and it leans toward the
answer. **Abstraction level is a dial on the fair axis**: concept of everything (~G1) <-
hypernym <- answer's basic category <- the answer itself (cheating). Worth running 2-3
rungs of the hypernym ladder on one family (brew: colour -> property -> concept) to see
the dial move.

## The table

Checked against each family README and sampled `items.json` golds. Both lineages' banks are
the same families; jle's dev bank v2 uses the same family keys.

| family | scored latent | task word | answer-class hypernym | notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| typo | the corrected word (February) | **typo** / misspelling | spelling / word | prompt-only floor is 1.00 here; report beside it |
| typo_mt | corrected multi-token form | **typo** | phrase; **number** for the 15 `tyh-arith-*` | |
| multilingual_typo | correction + language | **typo** | word + **language** | language is a scored unit: check subtraction doesn't hurt it |
| basic_readout | obvious next concept | **answer** | per subfamily: **fact** (entity), **number** (processing), **preference** (implicit) | subfamily-level words are still label-light |
| basic_readout_mt | multi-token next concept | **answer** | **name** (dynasties, compounds, processes) | |
| multihop | silent bridge (iron, May) | **fact** (prompts literally start `Fact:`) | **entity** / referent | bridge = referent of a descriptive phrase |
| multihop_mt | multi-token bridges (Simula 67) | **fact** | **name** | |
| multilingual_multihop | bridge, en/zh form | **fact** | **name** + language | |
| multilingual | English concept of the answer | **translation** | **meaning** / concept | latent is language-independent by design |
| multilingual_mt | concept + language | **translation** | concept + **language** | |
| arithmetic_intermediates | unwritten intermediate (−51) | **arithmetic** / calculation | **number** | |
| chain_intermediates | chain intermediates | **arithmetic** | **number** | |
| brew_intermediates | colour after first stir | **puzzle** / rules | **colour** | cleanest hypernym in the bench: 12-word palette; best family for the hypernym-ladder probe |
| association | unnamed implied concept (carnaval, chess, child) | **scene** / evocation | **concept** / theme | golds too heterogeneous for a tight hypernym; task word is the real arm here |
| conjunctive_association | compound state ("grief over … death of her child") | **story** / vignette | **emotion** / emotional state | contrast pairs differ in the state word (grief vs guilt) |
| role_bound_association | directed relation (who chased whom) | **story** | **action** / event | binding is the latent; a single word can't carry direction — expect null, itself informative |
| directed_modulation | held / suppressed concept | **instruction** / secrecy | **thought**; **secret** for secret+preference items | DM read cells vary -> abstract mu must ride on tok1/ctr-tok, not alone |
| multi_concept_directed_modulation | 1-3 held concepts + binding | secrecy | **thought** / imagined scene | |
| moral_rationale | the consideration the model weighs | **dilemma** / ethics | **reason** / value | deliberative items hold two reasons |
| buggy_code | the bug (or none, on clean twins) | **code** | **bug** / error | clean twins: subtracting "bug" must not *induce* bug reports — a precision check for free |
| hallucination | — (precision instrument) | conversation / chat | — | no target latent; only sanity-check that centring doesn't raise the rate |

| baselines | — (floors, not a family) | — | — | |

## Construction recipe (proposed)

1. **Carrier capture.** h_l at the last token of the word in k neutral carriers:
   `"typo"`, `"a typo"`, `"Concept: typo"`, `"Think about typos."` (plain render, matching
   the family's render where possible); average over carriers.
2. **Contrastive (steering) variant.** Same carriers with a neutral placeholder word
   ("thing") subtracted out: v = mean_c[h(c, word)] − mean_c[h(c, "thing")]. Removes the
   carrier's own template/token prior, leaving the concept direction. This is the README's
   "steering vector" reading.
3. **Magnitude.** mu = alpha * v with alpha tuned on dev bank v2 only (the real mean has
   ||mu||/||h|| = 0.81-0.98; an isolated word rep will not land there by luck). alpha = 1 and
   alpha matching the family-mean norm are the two pinned defaults.
4. **Composition.** Abstract mu alone is not token/position matched, so the arm of record
   is additive: mu = G2(token) + alpha * v_concept, with v alone as a diagnostic arm.

## Position: nothing to subtract literally, so condition the mean on it

README line 13 says "look into positional embeddings". Qwen3.6-27B (like all Qwen decoder
models) uses **RoPE**: position enters by rotating Q/K inside every attention block. There
is no additive positional-embedding vector in h_l, so "remove the position embedding" has
no literal reading here (in a GPT-2-style model you could subtract `W_pos[p]`; not in this
one). What exists instead is position-*correlated* structure that attention and MLPs write
into the residual: x101 already hit it ("the first positions carry outsized norms", hence
its MIN_POS cutoff — the attention-sink region), and the mention-control result (separation
only at sentence-final "." cells) is position structure too.

The functional analogue is a **position-conditioned corpus mean**:

    P:  mu(l, p) = E_corpus[ h_l | position p ]        (binned / smoothed over p)

- This is the *fair* cousin of carpos (same sentence, same position), which won on DM but
  failed the mention control because its reference reads the prompt. P's reference is
  neutral corpus text, so it carries no prompt content by construction.
- **Coordinate choice matters.** Two candidates: absolute index (captures the sink region
  and early-position norm decay) and **distance from end of prompt** (likely the right
  coordinate for bench reads at final-prompt tokens, where "2 tokens before generation
  starts" is the shared situation). Run both; absolute p pooled into log-spaced bins
  beyond ~64.
- **P vs G2.** Tokens and positions are correlated on bench (template tokens sit at fixed
  offsets from the end), so G2 may already absorb most of P there; the families where read
  cells vary (DM, agentic_misalignment, user_modeling, hallucination) are where P can add
  something G2 cannot. The joint (token, position-bucket) mean G2xP is the finer rung but
  needs more reference tokens per cell (sparsity — watch n per bucket).
- **Implementation is small**: `x101_generic_mean.py`'s accumulator already holds
  `[n_layers, n_pos, d]` residuals per passage and keys float64 sums by token id; add a
  per-position (and per token x pos-bucket) sum alongside. `jle/out/` is not live, so the
  means must be regenerated anyway (pod for 27B; 4B/9B were jle's local models).

The decomposition in "Why this arm is worth running" then gains a term:

    mu_fam  ~=  token prior (G2)  +  position prior (P)  +  category direction (alpha*v)  +  residual

per synthesis, but spills were not imported — check what is live before planning pod time.
Register predictions per `jle/notes/predictions.md` before judging. Headline read: how much
of (fam − G2) do P and alpha*v each recover on top of G2, per family.

1	# Pre-registered predictions (top-level jlm experiments)
2	
3	Continues the convention of `jle/notes/predictions.md` (kept light, per `notes/eval-pipeline.md`):
4	every prediction is written here with a timestamp BEFORE the confirmation run; never edited after
5	seeing results; outcomes are appended underneath. Experiment ids are `x1`, `x2`, ... (top-level
6	series, distinct from jle's x89+).
7	
8	---
9	
10	## x1-mu-pos-concept — REGISTERED 2026-10-10 15:45 BST (typo, 27B, strict free tier: the README's two
11	untried mu rungs — a position-conditioned corpus mean, and the abstract-word / steering mu)
12	
13	Instrument. The jlm pipeline on this box (3x A100; captures, reads and scores all local, dirty tree —
14	hashes instead of a SHA: centres.py dca1004d3d034e60, capture_mu_refs.py ea74f2b96786098b,
15	x1_arms.sh badfe51a37959add, evaluate.py abd34e2376ad9758; tests 11 pass). Banks: `data/dev/typo`
16	fit (94) / val (93); strict rule and confirmatory subset as in jle x89 (fit scored n=92, 2 leaks).
17	New centres: `pos@corpus` = mean at the same absolute position over 256 wikitext-103-VALIDATION
18	paragraph starts (x101's corpus, pin and detok; positions 0..63, every position; >= 8 cells else the
19	corpus mean); `fam@corpus8` / `tok@corpus8` = corpus / same-token mean from position 8 (x101's
20	MIN_POS); `fam@sents` = mean at the final token of 256 standalone wikitext sentences;
21	`cpt[c]:<word>:<alpha>@fit` = alpha x (fit-ref mean state norm) x unit carrier direction of <word>
22	(5 neutral carrier phrases, read at the word's last token; `c` subtracts the neutral words'
23	giraffe/violin/glacier carrier mean). Qwen3.6 is RoPE (+ gated-delta linear-attention blocks): there

content.thinking:
This is a rich prior. The abstract-mu work shows that concept steering vectors (abstract word representation, minus neutral placeholder) can help the centred readout, but the family mean (own-family mean) is much stronger.

But wait — this is all for the *27B* model and for *centring* (subtracting mu from the readout), in a local pipeline. The *current task* is different:
- 4B model
- Steering vector added to the forward pass (not subtracting from the readout)
- The readout remains plain (uncentred)
- Metric: strict pass@10 (0.1275 baseline), must reach ≥ 0.5.

Now, the current task's metric is important. The mean log10 rank is 2.33, meaning average rank ~213. To reach pass@10 ≥ 0.5, I need to bring a good fraction of the 102 items' targets into the top 10.

Let me think about why the plain read is SO bad here (0.1275 on 4B) versus the 27B "zero" arm (0.54-0.68). This is a big gap. Some of it is model size (4B vs 27B), but the read layers also differ (26/28/30 vs 20-60). Wait, the 4B model has 32 layers (n_layers=32), and the read layers are 26, 28, 30 — the top of the model, near the final norm. For the 27B (64 layers), reads were at 20-60.

Actually the plain read pass@10 = 0.1275 is a very low baseline. Let me think about what could get it to 0.5.

Key nuance: The J-lens read at layers 26/28/30 of the 4B, uncentred. The family mean centre gives huge gains. Since I can't center, I need to add a steering vector. Here's the thing though: adding a vector v at the read layer is a *constant* shift in state space and a constant shift in readout space. It cannot be item-specific. So the best I can do with a single vector is:

readout_t' = readout_t + (J_l v)_t normalized by something.

Actually for "cos" readout: score_t = (W_U J_l (h+v))_t / ||J_l^T W_U[t]|| = score_t(h) + (W_U J_l v)_t / ||J_l^T W_U[t]||.

So adding v adds a fixed per-token bias b_t = (W_U J_l v)_t / denom_t to every item's readout. This helps if b_t is high for the target token of that item — but targets differ. So a single vector can only help by:
(a) suppressing the tokens that universally rank above targets (the continuation prior), and/or
(b) boosting tokens that are commonly targets (association answers are activities/concepts — diverse, so hard).

Hmm. The continuation prior is the dominant problem. If I choose v such that b_t strongly suppresses `<|im_end|>`, newline, "The", "This", etc., then every target's rank improves by how many of those prior tokens were above it. But those are maybe ~5-10 tokens. Getting from rank 213 to rank 10 requires much more.

Wait — maybe I'm misunderstanding the metric. Let me reconsider "strict pass@10". In `read.py`, rank is computed over the whole vocabulary: rank = count of tokens with score > target's score. So the target is ranked within ~150k vocab. Mean rank 213 means on average only ~212 tokens beat the target. To get into top-10, need to make the target beat ~200 tokens. That's a big lift.

Wait, actually mean log10 rank = 2.3277 → mean(log10(rank+1)) = 2.3277 → geometric-mean rank ≈ 10^2.3277 ≈ 213. But that's the log-mean; the arithmetic mean rank could be much larger (dominated by high ranks). But pass@10=0.1275 means 13/102 items have rank ≤ 9. So ~89 items have rank ≥ 10, i.e., at least 10 tokens beat their target.

Hmm, this is a hard task. Baseline 0.1275. The centred read (own-family mean) would be the gold standard. Can I replicate it with a steering vector? Let me think harder.

The own-family mean mu = mean over association fit items of h at the read cell. The centred read J_l(h - mu). To replicate with steering, I'd add v = -mu at the read position. Then readout = J_l(h - mu), exactly the centred read. That would give ~0.6-0.7 (if the 4B centring works similarly). But v = -mu is "subtracting a mean" — forbidden.

BUT the rule says: "Directions, not means: each vector has to come from a contrast between two conditions (prompts or items you choose)." And "captures of other families' items through capture" are fine.

So a legal construction: v = mean(states where model is about to produce a one-word answer) - mean(states where model is continuing prose). This is a contrast direction, NOT a mean. If I pick the two conditions cleverly, v might approximate -mu + something.

Actually, here's a cleaner idea. The uncentred read problem: J_l h includes J_l mu_0 where mu_0 is the "expansion around 0" offset. Actually no, let me re-derive.

The J-lens: f(h) ≈ J_l h + c, where the model's next-token logits ≈ W_U · norm(J_l h + c) (ignoring final norm's Linearity... actually the final norm is RMS norm, nonlinear). The "cos" readout of the J-lens at layer l is (W_U J_l h)_t / denom_t. That's a linear approximation of logits minus the constant term c. So the plain read approximates logits but without the additive constant c (the "bias" term of the linearization around 0).

Centring at mu: J_l(h - mu) = J_l h - J_l mu. This readout approximates f(h) - f(mu). If mu is the "typical" read state (mean over items), then f(mu) is the "typical" continuation, and subtracting it isolates what's special about THIS item.

So the centred read works because it removes f(mu), the "typical" continuation (which includes the continuation prior). The uncentred read fails because it's missing the constant c, i.e., it's shifted by c relative to actual logits, and the magnitude of this error is huge.

Hmm wait, actually the uncentred read IS J_l h. The actual logits are (roughly) J_l h + c where c is the linearization constant. So the uncentred read is off by c from the actual logits. The "cos" readout, however, is normalized per token, and c is a constant... no wait, c is a constant VECTOR (over the vocab). Under cos readout, the score is (W_U J_l h)_t / denom_t, and the "missing" term would be (W_U c)_t / denom_t — a per-token constant offset.

So the plain read's per-token offset vs actual logits is essentially the continuation prior (which tokens the model tends to output on average). Removing it = centring.

To replicate centring with a steering vector: I want readout' = readout - (W_U J_l mu)_t / denom_t. Since adding v gives readout' = readout + (W_U J_l v)_t / denom_t, I need (W_U J_l v)_t = -(W_U J_l mu)_t for all t, i.e., v = -mu. That's a mean.

But here's the trick: I can build v = -mu as a CONTRAST. Consider v = mean(neutral/prose condition) - mean(answer condition). If the "answer condition" mean ≈ mu (the association read state mean) and "neutral/prose condition" mean ≈ 0-ish... no.

Actually, the contrast reads differently. Let me think about it as: v = mean_A - mean_B. Adding v: readout' = readout + J_l mean_A - J_l mean_B. So it's readout - J_l mean_B + J_l mean_A. If mean_B ≈ mu (the contaminating mean) and mean_A ≈ 0... but mean_A can't be 0 (it's a mean of states).

Hmm, alternatively: I want to ADD a vector that subtracts the "prose continuation" direction. The continuation prior is the direction of "the model continuing to write text". A contrast between:
- Condition A: "the model is NOT continuing prose" (e.g., it's about to end its turn / give a terse answer).
- Condition B: "the model is continuing prose" (the default prior state).

v = (state about to end turn) - (state mid-prose). Adding v pushes every read state away from "prose continuation" toward "turn ending". And since the read state h for an association item IS "about to end turn with the answer", adding v would... hmm, but the read position is the final token of the *prompt*, before the model generates. So the read state is "just finished reading the prompt, about to generate the answer". 

I think the cleanest and most defensible approach, and the one actually likely to work, is:

**Build v = (answer-once direction): mean of states at "the model is about to output a single-word answer" minus "the model is about to continue writing prose".** Both conditions constructed with my own prompts via `capture`.

But I'm worried about whether this actually moves pass@10 from 0.13 to 0.5. Let me get empirical quickly.

Actually, wait. There's a subtlety I should check: the positions argument. The vector is added at "prefix", "read", or "context" positions. What's the difference in effect on the read?

- "read": added at the read position only (the final token). Effect: readout += J_l v (direct, at read layer), and also propagates forward if read layer < final layer. But read layers are 26/28/30 and model has 32 layers, final norm at layer 31. So if I add at the read position but at layer 26, then the state flows through layers 27-31 before the final readout... but the J-lens reads at layer 26 output directly (the state at that point). So adding at (layer, read position) shifts that readout directly.

Actually the J-lens reads the residual stream at layer l output. Adding v at layer l output means the state read at layer l IS h_l + v. So readout at layer l = J_l (h_l + v) = J_l h_l + J_l v. Good, that's the direct effect.

- "prefix": added at context/prefix positions (earlier tokens). This changes all subsequent hidden states through attention, which can have a more "semantic" effect (steering the model's computation) but it's nonlinear and harder to reason about.

- "context": added at the context positions (the prompt tokens, excluding the read token presumably).

For a clean "replicate the centring" effect, "read" position is best: direct additive bias to the readout.

Actually, let me reconsider. The key realization: adding a vector at the read position at read layers 26/28/30 is EXACTLY equivalent to adding a constant to the readout. So the entire search space of interventions reduces to: choose a per-layer vector v_l, and its effect on the readout is a per-token constant bias b_l(t) = (W_U J_l v_l)_t / denom_l(t). The optimal such bias (to maximize target ranks) would boost target tokens and suppress others — but targets are diverse and unknown.

However! Here's the crucial additional consideration: the readout at layers 26/28/30 are *pooled or combined* somehow? Let me check how the metric server combines read layers. "strict pass@10 on association's fit split, read with the plain J-lens at layers 26, 28, 30". Maybe it averages the readout scores across the three layers, or takes the best layer, or ranks per layer then combines. The `read.py` computes rank per (item, layer, pos). The bench judge picks... hmm. Let me check how the strict rule combines layers.

Actually, for "strict pass@10", from read.py: rank is computed per (item, layer, pos). A cell "passes" if its rank ≤ 9 (top-10). The item passes if ANY of its read cells (across layers and positions) passes? Or the readout is aggregated?

Let me check the judge for the association family (basic judge). Let me look at wsbench evals/association or basic judge. Actually the bench judge for single-token families: "the default judge reads only the render's final token". Let me find how ranks across layers are combined into a per-item pass.

Let me look at wsbench/basic judge.

def cap(name, prompts, positions="last"):
    p = Path(f"out/steer/caps/{name}.pt")

    print(f"captured {name} n={out['n_prompts']} pos={positions}", flush=True)
    return {int(k): v.float() for k, v in out["mean"].items()}

def fam(name):

# Two-depth contrast steering for the plain J-lens read

The intervention adds two contrast directions to the residual stream, at different depths, at the read token only (position `read`). Both are built entirely from prompts I wrote and from position contrasts; no association target, answer, or item is used anywhere.

Inquiry deflection (layers 4-20).** I capture the residual state of forty self-written scene sentences in two conditions: bare ("She swung the racquet and watched the ball clear the net.") and wrapped as an explicit one-word question ("What activity is being described? Answer in one word. …"). The direction is the mean-state difference between the two conditions. Injected early, it tilts the forward pass toward naming the implied concept instead of continuing the prose, so the top-of-model state carries the answer as its next token.

**2. Continuation-prior deflection (layers 26-30).** The uncentred read J_l h is dominated by a sentence-final continuation prior. I contrast the mean mid-sentence residual with the mean sentence-final residual (an `all`-positions minus `final`-token capture over neutral prose). Adding this direction subtracts the final-position prior while leaving the mid-sentence baseline, exposing the per-item deviation that carries the target.

On association `fit`, the combined vector raises strict pass@10 from 0.1275 to 0.196 and lowers the mean log10 best-target rank from 2.33 to 2.06, applied at scale 1.0.

I've completed my work on this task. Here's a faithful summary of what happened and where it ended up.

## What I did

The task required an intervention that improves the **plain (uncentred) J-lens** read on association's `fit` split from a baseline of **pass@10 = 0.1275** to **≥ 0.50**, using only a steering vector (one vector per layer, added at `prefix`/`read`/`context`), built as a *contrast* between two conditions — no means, no association targets.

I explored the mechanism empirically through the metric server's `capture`/`run_metric` endpoints:

1. **Established the failure mode** — the plain read is dominated by a sentence-final continuation prior (top tokens are `The/At/When/This/They/But/Inside/Within/…`), with targets buried at rank ~10–200+.
2. **Constant read-cell bias** (subtracting a "prior" direction at layers 26/28/30) gave ~0.157 — matching the diagnostic that subtracting the sentence-final mean helps, but only weakly.
3. **Context/prefix steering** (instruction "answer mode" directions) was fragile and mixed (~0.12–0.16).
4. **Best result: a two-depth combination** — an *inquiry-deflection* direction at layers 4–20 (bare scene vs. scene+question contrast) plus a *continuation-prior deflection* at layers 26–30 (`all`-position vs. `final`-position contrast), both at the `read` cell.

## Final submission

- `submission/vectors.pt` — 8 layers (4,8,12,16,20,26,28,30), scale 1.0, position `read`
- `submission/contribution.md` — documents the two contrast directions (219 words)
- **Result: pass@10 = 0.1961** (baseline 0.1275), mean log₁₀ rank 2.06 (baseline 2.33). All four tracked examples improved (crater 10→5, airport 27→12, tragedy 45→22, flood 72→28).

## Honest verdict

The submission passes all structural checks (`test_fields`, `test_contribution`, `test_score_reproduces`), but **fails `test_performance`**: 0.1961 < 0.50.

My strong conclusion after ~20+ server-runs: the gain that reaches 0.5 is exactly the **own-family-mean centring** (`J_l(h − μ)`), whose effect can only be replicated by adding `v ≈ −μ` — an association-family mean the rules forbid. Every legal *contrast* proxy I could construct (neutral/scene sentence-final prior, other families' read cells, question-vs-continue, position contrasts, instruction steering) plateaus around **0.16–0.20**, because the association-specific "item-level read-cell content" that carries the family mean's gain is precisely what the rules prevent me from capturing. The intervention is genuine, novel, and rule-compliant, but the 0.50 threshold appears unreachable without the forbidden centring term.
